[[[null,["28a7fe28-01ab-4c19-952d-4cc266207ec4",["1791263136",964263000],["1791263129",926446000],["FluentFlow","Master English through interactive lessons, personalized practice, and real-world conversation exercises designed for all skill levels.","leaning english",null,"default",null,null,1,[1],null,[2]],1,[1,1,1]]],[null,["b46fa0cd-d34f-49c8-92e4-76f74ca6e74a",["1773706975",7260000],["1773663755",205136000],["workflow pod controller",null,"Design a kiosk tablet UI (1280x800 landscape, 10.1" screen) for a silence pod booking display. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  Layout                                                                                                                                                                                           

  Top Status Bar (full width, 40dp height):
  - Left: App name "Chamber Pod" + Device ID "SILENCE-POD-0001"
  - Center: Current time (HH:mm)
  - Right: Temperature "25°C", Humidity "45%", presence indicator (green dot), settings gear icon

  Main Content (two-column split):

  Left Column (55% width):

  Pod Banner Card at top:
  - Pod name: "Silence Pod A3"
  - Floor 2, Location: "Building B, Zone 3"
  - Capacity: 4 people (icon + text)
  - Status badge: green "Available" or red "In Use"

  Upcoming Bookings List below banner (scrollable):
  - Each booking card shows:
    - Time range bold: "14:00 - 15:00"
    - Meeting title: "Sprint Planning"
    - "Booked by: John Nguyen"
    - "Participants: 3" with people icon
  - Currently active meeting card has a highlighted blue left border
  - Show 3-4 booking cards in the list
  - If no bookings, show empty state: "No upcoming bookings"

  Right Column (45% width):

  Current Meeting Panel (large, prominent):
  - Header: "Current Meeting" label
  - Large meeting title: "Sprint Planning"
  - "Booked by: John Nguyen"
  - Time: "14:00 - 15:00"
  - Countdown: "45 min remaining" in accent color
  - Large QR code (200x200dp) centered, on a white square background for contrast
  - Text below QR: "Scan to check in"

  Quick Controls Row at bottom of right column:
  - 3-4 circular icon buttons in a row: Light bulb, Fan, Lock, Desk
  - Each toggleable with on/off state (blue when on, gray when off)

  Bottom Navigation Bar (full width, 48dp):
  - Two tabs: "Bookings" (calendar icon, active/highlighted) and "Controls" (sliders icon, inactive)

  Style Notes

  - Material 3 dark theme, rounded corners (12dp) on all cards
  - Card borders: subtle #3A3A3A
  - Clean, minimal, no gradients
  - Monospace or sans-serif font
  - This is a kiosk display meant to be viewed from standing distance

  Generate a high-fidelity mockup of this screen",null,"default",null,"1507",1],1,[1,1,1]]],[null,["fb02c7b2-7b75-4ef4-a9cc-f320b5a6bb72",["1773660452",837722000],["1773656673",821865000],["WorkFlow POS progressive web app (pwa)",null,"To redesign this administrative portal as a Tablet-Friendly Progressive Web App (PWA), you need to shift from a "point-and-click" desktop mindset to a "touch-and-swipe" mobile mindset.
Here is a strategic redesign guide based on the four screens you provided:
1. General UX Principles for Tablet PWA
Touch Targets: Every button, checkbox, and dropdown must be at least 44x44px to prevent "fat-finger" errors.
Gestures: Incorporate swipe-to-delete or pull-to-refresh.
Split-Screen Layouts: On tablets (especially in landscape), use a Master-Detail pattern (List on the left, details on the right) instead of long vertical forms.
Offline Mode: Since it's a PWA, ensure basic functions (viewing the schedule or customer list) work without internet.
2. Screen-by-Screen Redesign Strategy
Image 1: Admin Dashboard
Current Issue: The "Quick Actions" are tucked away on the right. Stats are small.
Redesign:
Action Grid: Move "Quick Actions" to the top as a horizontal scrolling row of large, colorful tiles.
Card Design: Increase the size of "Total Users" and "Active Bookings" cards. Use sparkline charts instead of just numbers to give immediate visual context.
Activity Feed: Use a full-width list with larger avatars for "Recent Activity."
Image 2: Create Space Booking
Current Issue: The horizontal "Schedule View" is very difficult to navigate on a touch screen.
Redesign:
Vertical Timeline: Switch the grid to a vertical scrollable timeline (Time on the Y-axis, Spaces on the X-axis).
Time Selection: Instead of typing numbers, use a "Drag-to-Book" interface where a user taps a slot and drags down to set the duration.
Sticky Header: Keep the "Customer Info" in a small collapsed bar at the top so the user always knows who they are booking for while scrolling through times.
Image 3: Topup Point
Current Issue: Massive amount of wasted white space on the right.
Redesign:
Two-Pane Layout: Put the Point Packages on the left (60% width) and a "Receipt/Checkout Summary" on the right (40% width).
Package Tiles: Make the 500k, 200k, etc., buttons much larger. They should look like physical cards that "press down" when tapped.
Floating Action Button (FAB): Place the "Create Topup" button as a fixed yellow button at the bottom right for easy thumb access.
Image 4: New Order Package
Current Issue: The multi-column layout looks cluttered. The "Order Summary" is too far from the "Select Products" section.
Redesign:
Stepper Navigation: Use a 3-step wizard: 1. Select Customer -> 2. Select Products -> 3. Payment. This reduces cognitive load on a smaller screen.
Visual Cart: Add a floating cart icon that shows the number of items. Tapping it opens a side-drawer (Modal) for the Order Summary.
Numpad Optimization: When clicking "Quantity," trigger a custom large on-screen numpad rather than the default system keyboard to keep the UI clean.
3. Proposed UI/Visual Changes
Navigation: Replace the thin left sidebar with a Bottom Navigation Bar (Home, Bookings, Orders, Users, More). This is standard for PWAs and easier to reach with thumbs while holding a tablet.
Typography: Increase base font size to 16px or 18px.
Feedback: Add haptic feedback (vibrations) on button presses to simulate a native app experience.
Color Palette: Keep the Workflow yellow, but use it more sparingly as an "Action Color" (Primary Buttons) and use soft grays for backgrounds to reduce eye strain for staff working long shifts.
4. Technical PWA Enhancements
Manifest File: Ensure the app can be "Added to Home Screen" with a high-res icon.
Service Workers: Cache the "Create Space Booking" assets so the form loads instantly even on spotty Wi-Fi in a large coworking space.
Camera Integration: Use the tablet's camera to scan QR codes for customer check-ins or membership cards.",null,"default",null,"964725",1],1,[1,1,1]]],[[[["FitNexus Admin","A modern, AI-powered administration dashboard for fitness centers featuring member management, class scheduling, and intelligent business insights.","build admin page for fitness gym
